_: The public demo's readers and their shared feeds, made by the web program on start when FORENOON_WEB_DEMO names a persona that is not an account yet. docs/demo.md says why each is here.

personas.name: Mara
personas.interests:
I write systems software: Rust mostly, some C and Zig, and I spend a lot of time inside databases and compilers. I want long technical posts that explain how something actually works: a storage engine's write path, a borrow checker's rules, a GC pause traced to its cause, a benchmark with the methodology shown. Postmortems and debugging stories are my favourite genre. Hardware is interesting when it changes how software is written (new memory hierarchies, SIMD, GPU programming models). I like the people side of this world too: how a team maintains a large codebase, how open source projects make decisions.

Skip: product launches and funding news, listicles, beginner tutorials, "10 tips" posts, anything about AI that is not a concrete engineering result, and general tech news unless it is about a security hole with real technical detail. One good 30-minute read beats five short ones.

personas.name: Theo
personas.interests:
I follow economics and public policy the way other people follow sport: housing and land use, energy and the grid, industrial policy, trade, central banks, how cities and institutions actually work. I want reported pieces and well-argued essays with data in them, from any side, and I like a long explainer on something unglamorous (permitting, transmission lines, procurement, pensions). History of institutions and infrastructure is very welcome. I will read a good piece on technology when it is about its economics or regulation rather than the technology itself.

Skip: hot takes, partisan point-scoring, market wraps and daily price moves, personal finance, and anything about crypto. A few genuinely major news events a week are enough; I am not trying to keep up with the day.

personas.name: June
personas.interests:
I read for pleasure: science writing, natural history, medicine, the history of ideas, and long reported features about people and places. I like a piece that follows one researcher or one question for a few thousand words, essays that take an unexpected angle, and good explanations of new results in physics, biology, climate or neuroscience written for an intelligent non-specialist. Book-length thinking in article form. Some technology is fine when it is about what it does to people.

Skip: press-release science ("study finds"), health advice, productivity and self-help, and anything that needs me to already follow a field's gossip. I want one or two important news stories only when something has really happened; otherwise no news at all.
